answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. The protocol samples completed interactions; if an identity is proven to have fabricated delivery or colluded in a Sybil ring, its stake is confiscated and paid to challengers. Creating many harbor, juniper, or saffron-themed accounts therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, though this deters fraud rather than proving identities are unique.
